findings.issue_text: [BUG] The non-immediate path of deleteScheduledEmailReminder never cancels the scheduled SendGrid send for reminders more than one hour out; it only sets cancelled=true in the DB and returns. handleCancelBooking.ts (lines ~485-490) calls this without immediateDelete, so a cancelled booking whose email reminder fires in >1 hour is never cancelled at SendGrid — the attendee still receives the reminder email for a cancelled booking, and the workflowReminder row is orphaned forever because the cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts only picks up cancelled rows with scheduledDate within the next hour.

[BUG] The rewritten deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are async DB-mutating functions invoked inside a forEach with no await, unlike the previous code which awaited Promise.all over the deletions. The booking-cancel handler returns before reminder rows are deleted; on a serverless platform the in-flight prisma.workflowReminder.delete calls can be killed after the response flushes, leaving dangling reminders for cancelled bookings, and any downstream code in the same request that reads workflowReminders sees stale rows.

[BUG] The remindersToCancel loop POSTs to SendGrid with reminder.referenceId as batch_id, but reminders with cancelled=true can have referenceId=null (they were marked cancelled before ever being scheduled), so the SendGrid request fails. The thrown error is caught by the outer try/catch after the first null referenceId, aborting the whole loop — all remaining cancelled reminders (including ones with valid referenceIds) are never cancelled at SendGrid and never deleted from the DB in that run, so already-cancelled bookings keep sending reminder emails.

[BUG] The condition changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, so the entire sendTo input block is no longer rendered when only a sender ID is needed. Users configuring an SMS step that requires only a senderId (SMS_SENDER_ID_ENFORCED / alphanumeric sender workflows) lose the input for steps.N.sendTo entirely and cannot save the workflow step, since the form field the schema requires has no UI to fill it.

[BUG] remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => {...}) fires async reminder deletions with no await before the mutation continues to reschedule reminders. The workflow update mutation returns and subsequent scheduling code runs while old reminder rows are still being deleted, so the new reminder scheduling and the old reminder deletion race — stale rows can survive or the newly-scheduled reminder can be deleted by the in-flight loop, producing duplicated or missing reminders for the edited step.

[ADVISORY] The type annotation Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[] is used purely to hold client query objects that are later awaited together, duplicating what the surrounding code already does with plain arrays of promises. The next maintainer of this cron must understand an obscure internal Prisma client type to modify the deletion loop; storing the awaited promises directly (as remindersToDeletePromise above already does) removes the type dependency entirely.

[BUG] The cancellation sweep only processes reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour, so cancelled reminders scheduled further out are never cancelled at SendGrid and their DB rows are never deleted. When a booking is cancelled/rescheduled, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets cancelled=true on the DB row; the actual SendGrid cancellation happens solely in this cron handler, which filters `scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, 'hour') }`. A reminder for a cancelled booking that is scheduled to send in more than one hour never matches the query, never gets the /v3/user/scheduled_sends cancel call, and never gets its row deleted — the attendee still receives the reminder email for a booking that no longer exists, on every booking whose cancellation happens more than an hour before the reminder time (the common case, since most reminders are hours or days out).

[BUG] A single cancelled reminder with a null referenceId throws inside the loop, aborting processing of all remaining reminders in the batch. The query selects all cancelled:true reminders within the hour, but the old guard `reminder.referenceId` check was dropped at the call sites, so unscheduled reminders (referenceId null, which deleteScheduledEmailReminder can leave with cancelled=true when its own update runs) reach `client.request({ body: { batch_id: null } })`, which throws; the for-loop breaks and the outer catch swallows it, so every reminder after the offending one in the list keeps its scheduled SendGrid email and its DB row — reminders for cancelled bookings are silently sent.

[ADVISORY] The immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but returns without deleting or flagging the DB row, leaking WorkflowReminder rows. Callers using immediateDelete=true (deleteWorkflow in workflows.tsx, reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts) leave rows in the WorkflowReminder table that are neither deleted (unlike the SMS manager, which always deletes) nor marked cancelled, so they are invisible to the scheduleEmailReminders cleanup query and accumulate forever; operators see stale reminder rows for deleted workflows/rescheduled bookings and any future reconciliation logic keyed on these rows misfires.

[ADVISORY] Changing the render guard from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` silently drops the sender-ID UI when only a sender ID is needed. Any SMS workflow step configuration where isSenderIdNeeded is true but isPhoneNumberNeeded is false (e.g. sending to the attendee's booked number with a custom sender) previously rendered this block's inputs; now the entire section is unmounted with no replacement rendered elsewhere in the diff, so users can no longer set the sender ID for those steps — a silent feature regression with no removal note or migration of existing values.

[ADVISORY] The cancellation query does not filter on method, so any cancelled non-email reminder row that enters the table is processed against SendGrid. The query selects cancelled:true rows regardless of reminder.method; if a WorkflowMethods.SMS row is ever marked cancelled (any future caller of a shared cancel path), this handler issues a SendGrid scheduled_sends cancel with a Twilio referenceId, which fails or cancels the wrong provider's message, and the catch swallows it while blocking the rest of the batch from processing.

[ADVISORY] No SMS equivalent of the deferred-cancel mechanism exists, and the diff contains no tests for the new cancelled-flag lifecycle. The diff introduces a new persistence state machine (cancelled=true, cron-based deferred email cancellation, branch on referenceId/immediateDelete) across five call sites with zero test files in the diff — no spec covers the cancelled-reminder-not-sent case, the >1-hour window, or the null-referenceId path; a regression in any of these silently emails attendees of cancelled bookings, which is exactly the failure this PR was meant to fix.

[BUG] The cancellation sweep in the email scheduling endpoint queries ALL cancelled workflowReminders regardless of method and cancels them via SendGrid's /v3/user/scheduled_sends, then hard-deletes them from the database. An SMS reminder with cancelled=true (e.g. from a Twilio-cancelled booking whose scheduledDate is within the next hour) gets its referenceId sent to SendGrid (a no-op cancel that fails or corrupts state) and is then deleted from WorkflowReminder without its Twilio message ever being cancelled — the SMS reminder fires and the DB row is gone, so it can never be cancelled later. This bug also means reminder-cancellation logic now lives in an unrelated scheduling endpoint rather than in the reminder managers, a placement not traceable to any stated requirement.

[BUG] The remindersToCancel query filters only on cancelled=true and scheduledDate, and the cancel request uses reminder.referenceId without a null check, while emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder explicitly guards the null-referenceId case. A cancelled email reminder that never got scheduled (referenceId null, which this same PR makes reachable by removing the referenceId guard at all call sites) reaches client.request with batch_id: null, throwing and aborting the whole cancellation loop inside the try, so every subsequent cancelled reminder in the list keeps its cancelled flag and is never hard-deleted by later runs of this sweep.

[ADVISORY] The per-reminder SendGrid cancel and the DB delete are wrapped in one try/catch whose only recovery is console.log, and deletes are collected then awaited only if no iteration threw. One failing SendGrid call (rate limit, transient 5xx) leaves all prior successful cancels' DB rows un-deleted (the Promise.all is skipped by the catch), so they are re-cancelled on every subsequent run indefinitely; operators see only a console.log with no retry or alerting. This inverted-retry loop is new behavior in this diff with no requirement calling for best-effort, silent-failure cleanup.

[ADVISORY] This PR about workflow-reminder lifecycle bundles an unrelated UI restructuring of the phone-number/sender-ID block: the wrapper condition changes from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, and the deeply nested JSX is flattened. When a step needs only a sender ID (isSenderIdNeeded && !isPhoneNumberNeeded), the entire containing block — including any future content placed there — no longer renders; the behavior change is not traceable to the reminder-management intent and arrives mixed with ~80 lines of pure re-indentation churn that buries it in review.

[ADVISORY] Roughly 60 lines of whitespace-only re-indentation in the test/demo booking section are included in this PR. Future archaeologists bisecting a regression in the preview-booking code cannot tell this PR's functional changes from noise because the diff is inflated with pure indentation churn that serves no requirement; it also signals the file lacks a formatter gate, making this recurring churn likely in follow-up PRs.

[ADVISORY] The deferred-deletion design (cancelled=true + hourly sweep in scheduleEmailReminders) is applied to email only; the SMS path in deleteScheduledSMSReminder still hard-deletes immediately, so the two reminder channels now have asymmetric cancellation semantics with no single source of truth for the cancel lifecycle. The invariant 'a cancelled reminder is never sent' is enforced differently per channel: email relies on every scheduler query filtering cancelled=true (only the email endpoint in this diff does), while SMS relies on immediate deletion. Any SMS scheduling path that runs between a cancelled-flag write and a delete, or any future caller copying the email pattern to SMS, sends a reminder the user cancelled; the asymmetry is under-scoped relative to the stated 'comprehensive reminder management' intent.

[BUG] The immediateDelete=true branch cancels the SendGrid batch and then returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaving permanent orphan rows. Every reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts:964-973) and every workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx:211, 517) cancels the email at SendGrid but leaves the row in WorkflowReminder with scheduled=true and cancelled=null forever; the cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts only queries cancelled=true, so these ghosts are never reaped and accumulate unboundedly, and any code counting/iterating a booking's workflowReminders sees reminders that will never fire.

[BUG] The reminder cancellation calls (external API + DB write) are launched inside a forEach and never awaited or included in the awaited Promise.all, unlike the old code which pushed the DB deletes into prismaPromises. The Next.js handler returns and the serverless function is frozen/killed before deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder complete, so cancelled bookings keep their SendGrid scheduled sends live and reminder rows stale — reminders fire for cancelled bookings.

[BUG] The for-loop over remindersToCancel is wrapped in a single try/catch, so one failing SendGrid cancel (e.g. an already-sent or invalid batch_id) throws and skips every subsequent reminder in the batch. A single bad referenceId poisons the whole cron run: all later cancelled reminders are neither cancelled at SendGrid nor deleted from the DB, so emails are sent for bookings the user cancelled — and the same failing row aborts every subsequent run, making the failure recurring rather than transient.

[BUG] The old code scoped DB deletes with booking.userId = ctx.user.id; the new code passes reminder.id directly to deleteScheduledSMSReminder/deleteScheduledEmailReminder which delete/update by bare id with no ownership check. The updateWorkflow and deleteWorkflow mutations now delete or flag any WorkflowReminder reachable from workflow steps with no user scoping — the ownership enforcement that existed on the DB write in this exact loop is silently dropped.

[BUG] Cancelling an email reminder no longer cancels at SendGrid immediately (default immediateDelete path only sets cancelled=true in the DB); actual cancellation is deferred to the scheduleEmailReminders cron, which only processes reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour. The old code cancelled the SendGrid batch synchronously on booking cancellation; now if the reminder's scheduledDate is more than an hour out it stays live at SendGrid until the cron eventually picks it up, and if it falls inside the cron's run interval it is sent before the cron cancels it — the attendee receives a reminder for a cancelled booking.

[ADVISORY] The reschedule flow exists in two parallel service paths with divergent semantics: handleNewBooking.ts:964-973 calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, referenceId, true) (immediate cancel, row orphaned) while bookings.tsx calls the same function with the default (DB flag only, no SendGrid cancel). The two reschedule entry points produce different data (orphan rows vs cancelled rows) and different SendGrid state for the identical domain event; the next maintainer changing one path will miss the other — the classic parallel-path drift this PR itself was fixing.

[ADVISORY] The cancelled flag was added as the email-cancellation mechanism, but SMS reminders are hard-deleted, so the same domain event (reminder cancellation) has two incompatible data representations: lingering cancelled=true rows for email and no rows for SMS. Any future feature that must reason about past reminders (audit, 'did we send this', re-scheduling logic) gets asymmetric answers depending on channel; consumers of workflowReminders must now filter cancelled everywhere or they treat dead email reminders as live.

[ADVISORY] deleteScheduledEmailReminder is now a three-mode function (delete-if-no-referenceId / flag-cancel / immediate-cancel) selected by an untyped boolean parameter, with the immediateDelete mode silently skipping the DB write — a state machine encoded as optional flags. Callers already pass contradictory flag combinations across this diff (true in three sites, default in four), and the mode where the DB row is intentionally not cleaned is indistinguishable at the call site from a mistake; a named enum or split functions would make the row-orphaning mode explicit and compile-visible.

[BUG] The reminder-cancellation for rescheduled bookings is fire-and-forget: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async functions invoked inside a synchronous forEach with no await, so the surrounding try/catch never catches their rejections. When a SendGrid/Twilio call or the prisma update inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder rejects, the error is swallowed (unhandled rejection) and the previous booking's reminders stay scheduled — the attendee of the old slot receives reminders for a booking that no longer exists, and the 'Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders' log the diff claims never fires.

[ADVISORY] The objective silently drifted from 'delete all reminders for cancelled bookings' (the deleted comment) to 'mark email reminders cancelled and defer actual SendGrid cancellation to the scheduleEmailReminders cron': deleteScheduledEmailReminder without immediateDelete only sets cancelled=true and never touches SendGrid, while SMS reminders are still hard-deleted. A cancelled booking's email reminder is only actually cancelled if/when the scheduleEmailReminders endpoint runs while the reminder is within 1 hour of its scheduled date; anyone cancelling a booking whose reminder is >1h out depends entirely on cron execution (which also swallows errors with only a console.log) — a missed or failing cron run means attendees still get emails for cancelled bookings.

[BUG] The cancellation sweep filters on scheduledDate lte now+1h, so cancelled reminders with a scheduledDate more than one hour in the future are never selected, never cancelled at SendGrid, and never deleted. Attendees whose bookings are cancelled more than an hour before the reminder fires keep receiving reminder emails whenever the reminder's scheduledDate never passes through the 1-hour window during a successful cron execution (cron downtime, endpoint not being called, or SendGrid error in the try block which skips all deletes) — the cancelled rows accumulate permanently.

[BUG] The condition was changed from (isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) to isPhoneNumberNeeded only, silently dropping the sender-ID UI branch with no replacement anywhere in the diff. Users who previously set a custom SMS sender ID on a workflow step lose access to that configuration surface entirely; existing sender-ID settings become unreachable and effectively dead configuration with no deprecation path.

[ADVISORY] The remindersToUpdate loop inside forEach(async ...) plus removal of the explicit deleteMany changed 'delete reminders from edited steps' into non-awaited deferred cancellation, and errors inside it are unhandled rejections. Editing a workflow step's timing no longer guarantees the old reminder rows are cleaned or their scheduled sends cancelled before new ones are scheduled; a race between the un-awaited cancellation and scheduleWorkflowReminders can produce duplicate or stale reminders for the same booking, and failures vanish without logging.

[ADVISORY] The updateWorkflow path replaced a deleteMany explicitly scoped with `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` with calls to deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id) / deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, ...) that delete WorkflowReminder rows by bare id with no ownership re-check. The old code re-verified at delete time that the reminder belonged to a booking owned by ctx.user.id; the new delete path trusts that remindersToDeletePromise is fully user-scoped, so if that fetch joins through team/eventType relations that surface reminders for bookings owned by other users (team workflows), a user updating a workflow deletes other users' reminder rows and cancels their scheduled SendGrid/Twilio sends — an ownership-scope regression a reviewer cannot rule out from the removed guard alone.

[ADVISORY] The new cancellation loop sends reminder.referenceId (nullable) as the SendGrid batch_id and logs raw errors with console.log. When a cancelled reminder has referenceId null (the new deleteScheduledEmailReminder path explicitly allows null referenceIds), the POST body sends batch_id: null to SendGrid, which errors and — because the whole loop is inside one try/catch — aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in the window and also skips every prisma delete, leaving cancelled email reminders live past their scheduled time and rows never cleaned up; operators see only a console.log line.

[BUG] deleteScheduledEmailReminder performs the DB write (cancelled: true or delete) inside the same try/catch as the SendGrid request, so a SendGrid failure leaves the WorkflowReminder row fully intact with scheduled: true and cancelled: null. When a booking is cancelled or rescheduled and the SendGrid cancel API call throws, the DB row is never updated or deleted; the cron endpoint only queries cancelled: true, so the reminder is never cancelled or cleaned, and the already-scheduled SendGrid email fires for a cancelled/rescheduled booking — the exact failure the old code's unconditional deleteMany prevented.

[BUG] deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row inside the same try block as twilio.cancelSMS, so a Twilio failure skips the DB deletion entirely. Cancelled/rescheduled bookings whose Twilio cancel call fails leave the SMS WorkflowReminder row scheduled: true and cancelled: null forever; no cleanup path ever touches it (the cron endpoint only handles EMAIL batches), so the scheduled SMS fires for a cancelled booking and the row orphans permanently.

[BUG] The reschedule path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true), which with immediateDelete cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without updating or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Every reschedule leaves the previous booking's EMAIL WorkflowReminder rows orphaned in the DB with scheduled: true, cancelled: null and referenceId pointing at a cancelled batch: the cron endpoint filters cancelled: true so it never cleans them, and the rows accumulate as dead data tied to the now-CANCELLED original booking.

[BUG] The cron's cancellation loop awaits client.request per-reminder inside one try block, so a single failed/exception-throwing cancel (including any reminder whose referenceId is unusable) aborts processing of all remaining remindersToCancel rows and skips their deletes for that run. A transient SendGrid error on one reminder leaves every subsequent cancelled=true reminder in that run un-cancelled at SendGrid and un-deleted in the DB; if that reminder's scheduledDate passes before the next successful cron run, the reminder email is sent for a cancelled booking despite the system having marked it cancelled.

[ADVISORY] The edited-steps path uses remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) so the deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are fire-and-forget and not awaited before the request returns. If the process dies or the request handler tears down between mutation and completion, reminders for edited steps remain scheduled at SendGrid with no cancelled flag, so the cron never reconciles them — a reminder fires with the stale step's content for bookings under the old configuration; also the old code's awaited deleteMany guarantee of completed cleanup is silently lost.

[BUG] deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but returns without deleting or marking the prisma.workflowReminder row, dropping the DB cleanup the callers relied on. The delete-workflow mutation (workflows.tsx) and deleted-step path in updateWorkflow call this with immediateDelete=true; after the provider cancel succeeds the WorkflowReminder rows stay in the DB forever as orphaned scheduled rows, so no path ever deletes them — silent partial success with unbounded row accumulation.

[BUG] Every failure inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder is caught and reduced to console.log, so callers (booking cancel, reschedule, workflow delete) return success even when the provider cancel and/or the DB write never happened. A user cancels a booking, the SendGrid cancel throws, and the reminder stays scheduled at the provider — the attendee still receives a reminder email for a cancelled booking, with no error surfaced anywhere except a console.log the operator will not see.

[BUG] The forEach calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting, so the handler resolves the cancel response before the reminder deletion/cancellation completes. On a serverless deployment the function can freeze/terminate right after responding, leaving provider-side scheduled sends active and DB rows undeleted for a booking the user was told was cancelled — attendees of a cancelled booking still get reminder emails. The previous code at least awaited the Prisma deletes via Promise.all.

[BUG] The try/catch around the forEach calling the async delete helpers is dead: forEach does not await the promises, so the catch block can never observe an async failure, and log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') is unreachable for real errors. If cancellation of the previous booking's reminders fails, reschedule completes with stale reminders still scheduled at SendGrid/Twilio and the error path designed to log it never fires — the reminder for the old time slot still sends and the failure is invisible.

[BUG] The cancel loop awaits each SendGrid request sequentially with no rate limit, then wraps all DB deletes in a single try/catch that logs to console and continues — a single provider failure aborts the remaining cancels and all DB deletes while the endpoint still returns 200. One 4xx/5xx from SendGrid mid-loop leaves the already-cancelled reminders un-deleted in the DB and the not-yet-processed cancelled reminders still scheduled at the provider; because those rows have cancelled=true they are also skipped by the normal scheduler, so they neither send nor get cleaned up, and the cron reports success.

[ADVISORY] The reschedule mutation fires the reminder-deletion promises without awaiting them, replacing the previously-awaited Promise.all of Prisma deletes with fire-and-forget calls. The tRPC mutation returns success to the user before reminder cancellation of the previous booking commits; on process exit or a swallowed internal error the old booking's reminders survive, and the user gets reminders for a slot they moved away from with no error shown.

[ADVISORY] Reschedule cancels the previous booking's email reminders with immediateDelete=true (no DB row deletion) but SMS reminders with the two-arg form (DB row deleted), an unexplained asymmetry. After a reschedule, email WorkflowReminder rows for the old booking accumulate in the DB while their SMS counterparts are deleted; anyone querying workflowReminder data (or the cancel-reminders cron in scheduleEmailReminders, which matches on cancelled=true) sees inconsistent state between channels and the orphaned email rows are never cleaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The deferred-deletion design (cancelled=true + hourly sweep in scheduleEmailReminders) is applied to email only; the SMS path in deleteScheduledSMSReminder still hard-deletes immediately, so the two reminder channels now have asymmetric cancellation semantics with no single source of truth for the cancel lifecycle. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The immediateDelete=true branch cancels the SendGrid batch and then returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaving permanent orphan rows. Every reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts:964-973) and every workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx:211, 517) cancels the email at SendGrid but leaves the row in WorkflowReminder with scheduled=true and cancelled=null forever; the cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts only queries cancelled=true, so these ghosts are never reaped and accumulate unboundedly, and any code counting/iterating a booking's workflowReminders sees reminders that will never fire.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The old code scoped DB deletes with booking.userId = ctx.user.id; the new code passes reminder.id directly to deleteScheduledSMSReminder/deleteScheduledEmailReminder which delete/update by bare id with no ownership check. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The reminder-cancellation for rescheduled bookings is fire-and-forget: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async functions invoked inside a synchronous forEach with no await, so the surrounding try/catch never catches their rejections. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The objective silently drifted from 'delete all reminders for cancelled bookings' (the deleted comment) to 'mark email reminders cancelled and defer actual SendGrid cancellation to the scheduleEmailReminders cron': deleteScheduledEmailReminder without immediateDelete only sets cancelled=true and never touches SendGrid, while SMS reminders are still hard-deleted. A cancelled booking's email reminder is only actually cancelled if/when the scheduleEmailReminders endpoint runs while the reminder is within 1 hour of its scheduled date; anyone cancelling a booking whose reminder is >1h out depends entirely on cron execution (which also swallows errors with only a console.log) — a missed or failing cron run means attendees still get emails for cancelled bookings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes cancellation semantics for email reminders: most call sites now invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete` (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `workflows.tsx`), and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` in that mode only does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` and does not cancel the SendGrid scheduled send. Actual SendGrid cancellation + DB deletion is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only processes `cancelled: true` reminders whose `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. That creates a verifiable window where a cancelled/rescheduled booking’s SendGrid scheduled email remains active and can still be delivered unless the `scheduleEmailReminders` endpoint runs successfully at the right time; SMS reminders are still cancelled/deleted immediately (`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` deletes the DB record and cancels Twilio if possible), making behavior inconsistent. This is a correctness regression relative to the previous immediate cancellation behavior shown in the removed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cancellation sweep filters on scheduledDate lte now+1h, so cancelled reminders with a scheduledDate more than one hour in the future are never selected, never cancelled at SendGrid, and never deleted. Attendees whose bookings are cancelled more than an hour before the reminder fires keep receiving reminder emails whenever the reminder's scheduledDate never passes through the 1-hour window during a successful cron execution (cron downtime, endpoint not being called, or SendGrid error in the try block which skips all deletes) — the cancelled rows accumulate permanently.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation sweep only selects cancelled reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour` (and no lower bound), then cancels them at SendGrid and deletes the DB rows. But most cancellation paths now call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete` (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, `workflows.tsx`), which only marks `WorkflowReminder.cancelled=true` and does *not* cancel the SendGrid scheduled send. That means a reminder cancelled days ahead relies on this endpoint running successfully during the ~1 hour before send time; if it doesn’t run in that window (downtime / request not made), SendGrid will still send the email despite the booking being cancelled, and the cancelled row won’t be deleted until the sweep runs. This is a correctness defect exposed by the diff’s new “defer cancellation until near send time” design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The remindersToUpdate loop inside forEach(async ...) plus removal of the explicit deleteMany changed 'delete reminders from edited steps' into non-awaited deferred cancellation, and errors inside it are unhandled rejections. Editing a workflow step's timing no longer guarantees the old reminder rows are cleaned or their scheduled sends cancelled before new ones are scheduled; a race between the un-awaited cancellation and scheduleWorkflowReminders can produce duplicate or stale reminders for the same booking, and failures vanish without logging.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the edited-steps cancellation uses `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... })` but the calls inside are not `await`ed, and `forEach` itself is not awaited. Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async (and may throw), this change makes cancellation/deletion best-effort and can lead to unhandled rejections. It also no longer guarantees old reminders are cancelled/cleaned before subsequent workflow reminder scheduling logic continues, creating a real race that can leave stale/duplicate reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The updateWorkflow path replaced a deleteMany explicitly scoped with `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` with calls to deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id) / deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, ...) that delete WorkflowReminder rows by bare id with no ownership re-check. The old code re-verified at delete time that the reminder belonged to a booking owned by ctx.user.id; the new delete path trusts that remindersToDeletePromise is fully user-scoped, so if that fetch joins through team/eventType relations that surface reminders for bookings owned by other users (team workflows), a user updating a workflow deletes other users' reminder rows and cancels their scheduled SendGrid/Twilio sends — an ownership-scope regression a reviewer cannot rule out from the removed guard alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the previous `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` guard was removed and replaced with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, ...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, ...)`. Those helpers now update/delete `WorkflowReminder` by bare `id` (`prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`) with no ownership predicate. Whether this is an actual authorization bug depends on how `remindersToDeletePromise` / the reminder fetches are scoped (not shown in the diff), but the diff does show a defense-in-depth ownership check was dropped at the deletion point and the helper performs unscoped deletes/updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new cancellation loop sends reminder.referenceId (nullable) as the SendGrid batch_id and logs raw errors with console.log. When a cancelled reminder has referenceId null (the new deleteScheduledEmailReminder path explicitly allows null referenceIds), the POST body sends batch_id: null to SendGrid, which errors and — because the whole loop is inside one try/catch — aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in the window and also skips every prisma delete, leaving cancelled email reminders live past their scheduled time and rows never cleaned up; operators see only a console.log line.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation loop unconditionally does `client.request({ body: { batch_id: reminder.referenceId, status: "cancel" }})` for each reminder in `remindersToCancel`. The diff shows `referenceId` can be `null` (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId: string | null, ...)` explicitly handles null), but this API handler does not guard against null and would send `batch_id: null`. Because the whole loop is wrapped in a single `try { ... for (...) { await client.request(...) ... } await Promise.all(...) } catch { console.log(...) }`, a single failure would jump to the catch and stop processing remaining reminders and also skip the Prisma deletes, leaving `cancelled` reminders uncleared. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteScheduledEmailReminder performs the DB write (cancelled: true or delete) inside the same try/catch as the SendGrid request, so a SendGrid failure leaves the WorkflowReminder row fully intact with scheduled: true and cancelled: null. When a booking is cancelled or rescheduled and the SendGrid cancel API call throws, the DB row is never updated or deleted; the cron endpoint only queries cancelled: true, so the reminder is never cancelled or cleaned, and the already-scheduled SendGrid email fires for a cancelled/rescheduled booking — the exact failure the old code's unconditional deleteMany prevented.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is partially mischaracterized (in the default path `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` there is no SendGrid call; it just `update`s `cancelled: true`). However, the diff *does* introduce the core failure mode for the `immediateDelete` path: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)` only performs the SendGrid cancel request and then `return`s without updating/deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row (and all of this is inside a try/catch). Call sites like `handleNewBooking.ts` (reschedule) and `viewer/workflows.tsx` (deleted workflow/step) pass `true`. If the SendGrid cancel call throws, the DB row remains with `scheduled: true` and `cancelled` unset, so the new cron cleanup in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` (which only queries `cancelled: true`) will never pick it up, and the scheduled email may still fire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row inside the same try block as twilio.cancelSMS, so a Twilio failure skips the DB deletion entirely. Cancelled/rescheduled bookings whose Twilio cancel call fails leave the SMS WorkflowReminder row scheduled: true and cancelled: null forever; no cleanup path ever touches it (the cron endpoint only handles EMAIL batches), so the scheduled SMS fires for a cancelled booking and the row orphans permanently.

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` in the same `try` block. If Twilio throws, execution jumps to `catch` and the Prisma delete is skipped, leaving the WorkflowReminder row intact. The diff adds an email-only cleanup path in scheduleEmailReminders.ts for `cancelled: true` reminders, but there is no analogous SMS cleanup, and the SMS delete function does not mark rows as `cancelled`, so a failure can leave stale scheduled SMS reminders in the DB indefinitely.

Every reschedule leaves the previous booking's EMAIL WorkflowReminder rows orphaned in the DB with scheduled: true, cancelled: null and referenceId pointing at a cancelled batch: the cron endpoint filters cancelled: true so it never cleans them, and the rows accumulate as dead data tied to the now-CANCELLED original booking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cron's cancellation loop awaits client.request per-reminder inside one try block, so a single failed/exception-throwing cancel (including any reminder whose referenceId is unusable) aborts processing of all remaining remindersToCancel rows and skips their deletes for that run. A transient SendGrid error on one reminder leaves every subsequent cancelled=true reminder in that run un-cancelled at SendGrid and un-deleted in the DB; if that reminder's scheduledDate passes before the next successful cron run, the reminder email is sent for a cancelled booking despite the system having marked it cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic wraps the entire per-reminder processing loop in a single `try { ... for (...) { await client.request(...) ... } ... } catch { ... }`. Because each iteration does an `await client.request(...)`, any exception for one reminder (e.g., bad/null `reminder.referenceId` passed as `batch_id`, or a transient SendGrid failure) will jump to the `catch` and abort processing of all remaining `remindersToCancel`, and also skip `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` so their DB deletes won't run in that execution. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The edited-steps path uses remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) so the deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls are fire-and-forget and not awaited before the request returns. If the process dies or the request handler tears down between mutation and completion, reminders for edited steps remain scheduled at SendGrid with no cancelled flag, so the cron never reconciles them — a reminder fires with the stale step's content for bookings under the old configuration; also the old code's awaited deleteMany guarantee of completed cleanup is silently lost.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the edited-steps path does `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` but never awaits the resulting promises (Array.forEach ignores returned promises). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but returns without deleting or marking the prisma.workflowReminder row, dropping the DB cleanup the callers relied on. In the diff, callers in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` now invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` when deleting a workflow and when deleting a step, and the prior explicit Prisma `deleteMany` cleanup was removed. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every failure inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder is caught and reduced to console.log, so callers (booking cancel, reschedule, workflow delete) return success even when the provider cancel and/or the DB write never happened. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cancel loop awaits each SendGrid request sequentially with no rate limit, then wraps all DB deletes in a single try/catch that logs to console and continues — a single provider failure aborts the remaining cancels and all DB deletes while the endpoint still returns 200. One 4xx/5xx from SendGrid mid-loop leaves the already-cancelled reminders un-deleted in the DB and the not-yet-processed cancelled reminders still scheduled at the provider; because those rows have cancelled=true they are also skipped by the normal scheduler, so they neither send nor get cleaned up, and the cron reports success.

The handler then continues (after the catch) and can still return success, leaving some reminders still scheduled at SendGrid and/or stale `cancelled=true` rows in the DB.
